title: Concepts of Social Stratification
text:
Social stratification describes a society's system of ranking its members into hierarchical layers. This unequal distribution of power, wealth, and prestige is inherent to social structures and tends to be passed down across generations.

The study draws heavily from various theoretical perspectives. Functionalism suggests that some inequalities are necessary because they motivate individuals to fill the most critical roles in society. Conversely, conflict theory argues that stratification is rooted in the exploitative relationships between groups, maintaining power for the dominant class at the expense of others.

Contemporary analysis often incorporates Bourdieu's concept of capital—economic, social, and cultural—to better explain accumulated advantage. These forms of capital allow certain groups to maintain structural dominance regardless of purely monetary wealth.
